notes.subject: car
notes.text: Older coverage uses a white car with black roof racks; the only white Google car in the Middle East.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Newer coverage often uses a white pickup with a trekker, frequently blurred. Its antenna sits mid-cab, versus left in Qatar.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Some modern coverage is a black car with a visible brake light; Israel has a similar one.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Typically flat desert; mountains appear only in the far east.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow edge lines with white or yellow middle lines; Jordan, Israel and Oman use these too.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Arabic script, and signs often add English because of tourism; Qatar and Oman do this too, Jordan rarely.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Many signposts have black-and-white stripes; Oman has them too.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Almost all curbs are striped, either black and white or black and yellow.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Dark brown wooden poles with three insulators evenly set on a horizontal bar; Oman is similar.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Homes are light-coloured stone, and sidewalks often use reddish stone.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Divided roads and roundabouts are very common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Despite the wealth, residential roads are sometimes unpaved.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Coverage is mostly limited to the northeast; Sir Baniyas Island is the only car coverage beyond it.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A skyline of many skyscrapers, including the world's tallest tower, marks the biggest city.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Light-coloured mountains to the east mark the north of one emirate.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mountains to the west and flat land to the east put you on the far-east Gulf of Oman coast.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue street name signs with a narrow metal border are specific to the largest emirate.
